## fleet ls

List every device with live resource availability.

```
fleet ls [OPTIONS] [NAMES]...
```

Example:

```bash
fleet ls --json
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAMES` | only these devices |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--json` | print JSON instead of a table, for scripts and agents |
| `--refresh`, `-r` | force a live probe |
| `--rescan` | also re-read software versions and folder sizes, which machines otherwise cache for 6 hours |
| `--wait` `SECONDS` | with --rescan: wait up to this long for the folder sizes it started measuring |
| `--online` | only reachable devices |
| `--discover` | list machines in your ~/.ssh/config and on your tailnet that are not added yet |
| `--hide` `NAME` | with --discover: never offer this one again; repeatable |
| `--unhide` `NAME` | with --discover: offer it again |
| `--all` | with --discover: include hidden ones |
| `--fields` `A,B,...` | with --json: only these keys of each machine, e.g. free_vram_mib,gpus,usd_per_hour |
| `--tag` `NAME` | only machines carrying this tag or fact; repeatable, and all must match |

## fleet show

Full detail for one device.

```
fleet show [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet show machine_A
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | defaults to this machine |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--json` | print JSON instead of a table, for scripts and agents |
| `--refresh`, `-r`, `--no-refresh` | probe it now; --no-refresh shows the last reading |
| `--rescan` | also re-read software versions and folder sizes, which machines otherwise cache for 6 hours |
| `--wait` `SECONDS` | with --rescan: wait up to this long for the folder sizes it started measuring |

## fleet add

Add a machine: how you reach it over ssh, or a name from `fleet ls --discover`.

fleet connects exactly as you do -- your ssh config, your keys and agent, Tailscale SSH, the key on your rental provider's account -- and installs nothing there.

```
fleet add [OPTIONS] [SSH_COMMAND]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet add "ssh -p 58418 root@1.2.3.4"
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `SSH_COMMAND` | e.g. "ssh -p 58418 root@1.2.3.4" |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--self` | record the machine you are on, with no ssh |
| `--name` | what to call it; guessed from the host if omitted |
| `--alias` `SHORT` | a short handle to type instead of the name |
| `--tag` `NAME` | label it; repeatable. `fleet ls --tag NAME` finds it again |
| `--kind` | permanent\|rental\|shared\|appliance\|mobile |
| `--json` | print JSON instead of a table, for scripts and agents |
| `--dry-run` | probe and show what would be recorded; record nothing |

## fleet edit

Change a device's address or settings after it was added.

Rentals recycle IPs and ports, so `--ssh` re-points a device without losing its name, tags, cost or history. Tags, cost, a note, folders (`--path`) and declared servers (`--endpoint`) are written to that machine's own machine.yaml, so everyone who looks at it reads the same; `--local` keeps tags and cost here instead.

```
fleet edit [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet edit machine_A --ssh "ssh -p 40001 root@5.6.7.8"
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | defaults to this machine |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--ssh` `CMD` | new address, e.g. "ssh -p 2222 root@5.6.7.8" |
| `--disk-path` `PATH` | watch this mount or directory for free space; repeatable |
| `--clear-disk-paths` | go back to autodetecting mounts |
| `--name` `NEW` | rename it; the id and its history stay |
| `--alias` `SHORT` | a short handle to type instead of the name; --alias "" removes it |
| `--tag` `NAME` | add a label; repeatable |
| `--untag` `NAME` | remove a label; repeatable |
| `--cost` `USD` | what it costs per hour, for the $/HR column and the fleet's burn rate; 0 clears it |
| `--note` `TEXT` | a line about the machine; --note "" clears it |
| `--path` `KIND=PATH` | where this machine keeps models, datasets, media...: models=/data/models; repeat a kind for several, models= clears it |
| `--endpoint` `NAME=PORT[/PATH]` | a model server fleet would not find by itself: myllm=9000 or myllm=9000/v1; myllm= removes it. Never a key |
| `--local` | keep --tag/--untag/--cost in this machine's own list instead of on that machine |
| `--json` | print JSON instead of a table, for scripts and agents |

## fleet install

Install fleet on a device, so you and its agents can use fleet from there too.

A machine fleet only looks at needs nothing installed; this is for one you also work on. It installs from git; re-running updates an existing install.

```
fleet install [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet install machine_A
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | the machine to install fleet on |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--repo` `URL` | git URL to clone; defaults to config or this checkout |
| `--ref` | branch or tag to install (default: `main`) |
| `--forward-agent`, `--no-forward-agent` | authenticate the clone as you, leaving no credential on the device; by default only for a git URL over ssh |

## fleet update

Update fleet on the machines that have it, the way it was installed there.

A machine with fleet from PyPI gets `uv tool upgrade` (or `pipx upgrade`), one with fleet's own checkout is updated from git, and your own source install is left as it is. `--repo` or `--ref` asks for git everywhere. Updates this machine without ssh, and `--all` every machine that runs fleet.

A device with no fleet is skipped and named, never given one: most of a fleet is meant to have nothing installed, and `fleet install NAME` is how you change that on purpose.

```
fleet update [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet update --all
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | defaults to this machine |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--all` | every device that already runs fleet |
| `--repo` `URL` | git URL to deploy from; defaults to config or this checkout |
| `--ref` | branch or tag (default: `main`) |

```

```


| Argument | |

|---|---|

## fleet top

Live view of the fleet, or of one device. Like htop, for your machines.

Anything unreachable backs off instead of being redialled every couple of seconds. Shared multi-user hosts are probed only when asked for by name (`fleet ls NAME`).

```
fleet top [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet top machine_A -i 1
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | one device, instead of the whole fleet |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--interval`, `-i` | seconds between refreshes (default: `2.0`) |

## fleet rm

Stop watching a machine: take it out of this machine's list.

Nothing is changed on the machine itself: what `fleet edit` wrote to its machine.yaml (tags, cost, a note, folders, servers), and fleet if you installed it there, stay with it.

```
fleet rm [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Example:

```bash
fleet rm machine_A
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` (required) | the exact name; a prefix is never enough |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--yes`, `-y` | do not ask for confirmation |

## fleet ssh

Open a shell on a device, or run a command: `fleet ssh machine_A -- nvidia-smi`.

The wrapper resolves the endpoint and connects exactly as you would, so an agent never needs an address, a key or a password -- only the machine's name.

```
fleet ssh [OPTIONS] NAME [-- COMMAND...]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet ssh machine_A -- nvidia-smi
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` (required) | a machine's name or alias |

## fleet wake

Wake a sleeping or switched-off machine with a Wake-on-LAN packet, and wait for it.

The packet is a broadcast on the machine's own network. It is sent from here when this machine is on that network, and otherwise by a fleet machine that is, over ssh -- so from anywhere, while one machine there is up. What the machine's cards are, and whether each is armed to wake, its last probe read; its machine.yaml can name the card instead (`wake: {mac: ...}`).

```
fleet wake [OPTIONS] NAME
```

Example:

```bash
fleet wake gpu-tower
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` (required) | a machine's name or alias |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--via` `NAME` | send the packet from this machine, which must be on the same network |
| `--no-wait` | send the packet and return, without waiting for it to answer |
| `--timeout` `SECONDS` | how long to wait for it to answer (default: `180`) |
| `--json` | print JSON instead of a table, for scripts and agents |

## fleet setup

Teach your coding agents to use fleet.

An agent with a shell gets a skill, which costs nothing until a task actually needs a machine. A desktop client has no shell, so it gets `fleet mcp` registered as an MCP server instead -- merged into its config beside whatever else is already there.

```
fleet setup [OPTIONS]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet setup --dry-run
```

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--target` | an agent name, or all \| auto (whatever is installed; the default); repeat it, or use commas, for several |
| `--project` | write into the current directory, not your home |
| `--dry-run` | show what would change; write nothing |
| `--uninstall` | remove what setup installed |
| `--refresh` | rewrite only what fleet already installed, so it matches this fleet; adds nothing new |

## fleet uninstall

Take fleet off this machine: out of your agents, and with --purge its files.

Nothing on the machines fleet looked at changes. The program itself is removed last, by you: the command to run is printed at the end.

```
fleet uninstall [OPTIONS]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet uninstall --purge
```

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--purge` | also delete fleet's files here: its list of machines, cache and logs |
| `--yes`, `-y` | do not ask; needed without a terminal |
| `--json` | print JSON instead of a table, for scripts and agents |

## fleet paths

Show where fleet keeps its state.

```
fleet paths [OPTIONS]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet paths
```

## fleet doctor

Why a machine will not let fleet in, and the one thing to do about it.

fleet connects exactly as you do and manages no access, so the fix is yours to make: usually putting your key on the machine, adding it to a rental provider's account, or a rule in your Tailscale SSH policy. This names the one for each machine. It changes nothing.

```
fleet doctor [OPTIONS] [NAME]
```

Example:

```bash
fleet doctor gpu-box
```

| Argument | |
|---|---|
| `NAME` | one machine; all that are failing if omitted |

| Option | |
|---|---|
| `--json` | print JSON instead of a table, for scripts and agents |
